title: Have you ever…?
goal: Talk about experiences — what you have, haven't and have just done — and know when to use this form instead of the simple past.
bekal: tell when to use the past and when to use the perfect
use *jo*, *vielä*, *koskaan* and *vasta* in the right places

dialogs.title: Dialog — Kaksi vuotta Suomessa
dialogs.intro: Two years since the first day of the course. Aino and Budi meet at the same café as back then.

lines.text: Olen oppinut paljon. Ja olen tullut kärsivällisemmäksi.

lines.text: Talvella. Olen asunut täällä kaksi vuotta enkä pelkää enää.

notes: **Olen oppinut** — *olla* plus a form you already know from past negatives. The *-nut/-nyt/-neet* ending you learned in unit 14 turns up again here, this time in positive sentences. Old practice pays off twice, just as promised.

**The difference from the past: is a time mentioned?** *Kävin Lapissa viime helmikuussa* — the time is specific, so past tense. *Olen käynyt Lapissa* — whenever, what matters is the experience, so the perfect. The same rule as in English: "I went last February" versus "I've been".
**En ole vielä tehnyt** — "I haven't done it yet". The negative: negative verb + *ole* + the *-nut* form. Note that *olla* becomes bare *ole*, just as in ordinary negatives.

**Olen asunut täällä kaksi vuotta** — the perfect is also used for things that are **still going on**. I've lived here for two years, and I still do. With the past (*asuin täällä kaksi vuotta*), the meaning changes: I used to live here, but not anymore.
**Olen juuri saanut** — *juuri* means "just". It's almost always paired with the perfect, not the past.

**Revontulia** literally means "fox fires" — *revon* (fox's) + *tulet* (fires). According to folklore, an arctic fox running fast swept its tail across the snow and sent sparks flying into the sky. It's one of the most beautiful Finnish words, and Finns love it when you know its origin.

grammars.title: The perfect ("have done")
body: Built from two parts: *olla*, which changes with the person, and the main verb in the **-nut/-nyt** form (one person) or **-neet** form (several people), which doesn't change any further.
after: The *-nut/-nyt/-neet* form is exactly the one used in past negatives. If you can say *en mennyt*, you can already say *olen mennyt* — just swap the negative verb for *olla*.
Asking: *Oletko käynyt…?*, *Onko hän ollut…?*. Answer by repeating *olla*: *Olen.* / *En ole.*
**There's a past version too** — *olin käynyt* (I had been, before something else happened). It's rarely needed at A1, but you'll recognize it when you see it.

grammars.title: Past or perfect?
body: The choice depends on one thing: **is a time mentioned, and is it over?** If so, use the past. If you're talking about an experience or a situation that still holds, use the perfect.

head: Past
Perfect
The difference
rows: one night / ever in my life

after: **Words that call for the perfect:** *jo* (already), *vielä* (yet, with a negative), *koskaan* (ever, with a negative), *aina* (always), *juuri* (just), *monta kertaa* (many times).
**Words that call for the past:** *eilen*, *viime viikolla*, *viime vuonna*, *kello seitsemän*, *silloin*, and any mention of a time that's over.
⚠️ If you're unsure at A1, **the past is safer**. Using it where the perfect belongs sounds a little less polished, but it's always understood; the reverse isn't always true.

blocks.text: ⚠️ Type 3 verbs (*tulla*, *mennä*, *nousta*, *opiskella*) double the last consonant of the stem and drop the *n*: *tul-lut*, *men-nyt*, *nous-sut*, *opiskel-lut*. The same pattern as in unit 14.

blocks.title: Four things Finns often ask newcomers
items: *Kuinka kauan olet ollut Suomessa?* — How long have you been in Finland?
*Oletko tottunut talveen?* — Have you got used to the winter?
*Oletko käynyt saunassa?* — Have you been to a sauna?
*Mikä on ollut vaikeinta?* — What's been the hardest?
All four use the perfect, and you'll hear all four dozens of times. Prepare your answers now, in Finnish, two sentences each.

exercises.prompt: Choose the past or the perfect.
items: ____ täällä kaksi vuotta ja asun edelleen. (asua, I)
____ Espoossa kaksi vuotta, sitten muutin. (asua, I)
How long have you lived here?

answers: Minä olen oppinut paljon. — Sinä olet käynyt Lapissa. — Hän on nähnyt revontulet. — Me olemme olleet siellä. — Te olette jo syöneet. — He ovat asuneet täällä.
En ole käynyt Lapissa. — Et ole nähnyt revontulia. — Hän ei ole tullut. — Emme ole päättäneet. — He eivät ole oppineet suomea.
Kävin — Olen käynyt — Olen asunut — Asuin — ole nähnyt
Oletko käynyt Lapissa? — En ole koskaan käynyt. — Olen oppinut paljon. — Olen juuri tullut. — Kuinka kauan olet asunut täällä? — Olen asunut täällä kaksi vuotta.
